en.title: AAPA urges Asia Pacific governments to back airlines as fuel crisis bites
en.summary: The Association of Asia Pacific Airlines closed its 70th Assembly of Presidents in Kuala Lumpur by calling on governments to give carriers timely, practical support as jet fuel trades near $186 a barrel, about a third of operating costs, with passenger traffic up 1.9% in the first nine months of 2026 but margins under severe strain.
body: The Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA) has called on governments across the region to provide timely, practical support to carriers facing sharply higher fuel prices and mounting operational hurdles. The appeal came at the close of its 70th Assembly of Presidents in Kuala Lumpur on November 13, 2026, a two-day event hosted by Malaysia Airlines that brought together more than 170 delegates under the theme "Redefining Aviation: Growth, Resilience and Innovation" and marked the association's 60th anniversary. "Governments must recognize these pressures and work constructively with the industry to provide support that safeguards the long-term viability of air transport across the region," said AAPA's Director General.

On the surface, demand has held up. Passenger traffic for Asia Pacific airlines grew 1.9% in the first nine months of 2026, and average load factors reached a record 83%. "Let's be candid. A full aircraft does not necessarily translate into a healthy bottom line!" AAPA's Director General told delegates during his opening address on November 13. Jet fuel was trading at around $186 per barrel in October, compared with $80 to $110 in recent years, and fuel now makes up about 33% of airline operating costs, with the jet fuel crack spread the widest the industry has seen in many years. "We have to consume fuel. We have to burn fuel. We have no alternatives, at least not now," he said, adding that airlines "end up being price takers." AAPA's aggregate passenger numbers were negative from April to August, before edging back "just above water" in September.

He stopped short of a specific wish list, urging governments instead to begin by benchmarking the taxes and fees they levy on airlines, such as departure taxes, landing fees and parking fees, against those of neighboring countries, and asking whether they are reasonable and actually support aviation. On fuel above $185 per barrel, he said: "That better not be the norm. If that's the norm, we have trouble. Not sustainable." He warned that if fuel prices stay where they are, "this could really be a problem," and said AAPA's biggest worry is a "snowball effect" in which one airline's distress spreads to others. The Assembly also adopted four resolutions covering aviation sustainability, passenger rights, cabin safety and aviation security, and reaffirmed a target of 5% sustainable aviation fuel use by 2030, though SAF still costs three to four times as much as conventional jet fuel.

zh.title: 亞太航空協會籲請各國政府出手相助、協助航空業度過燃油危機
zh.summary: 亞太航空協會在吉隆坡舉行的第70屆會長大會閉幕時呼籲各區政府及時以實際行動支援航空公司；10月噴射燃油每桶約186美元、占營運成本約33%，2026年前9個月亞太航空客運量雖成長1.9%、平均載客率創83%新高，業者獲利仍備受擠壓。
body: 亞太航空協會在2026年11月13日於吉隆坡舉行的第70屆會長大會閉幕時，呼籲各地區政府為面臨燃油價格急升與營運障礙加劇的航空公司提供及時、實際的支援。這場為期兩天的會議由馬來西亞航空主辦，170多名代表與會，同時慶祝協會成立60周年。協會總幹事表示，各國政府必須正視這些壓力，與業界建設性合作，提供支援以維護本地區航空運輸的長期存續。
需求表面上仍穩健：2026年前9個月亞太航空客運量成長1.9%，平均載客率達83%的歷史新高。協會總幹事在11月13日的開幕致詞中坦言，客機滿載未必代表獲利健康。噴射燃油10月每桶約186美元，遠高於近年每桶80至110美元的水準，燃油現占航空公司營運成本約33%，煉油價差也是多年來最寬。他指出，航空公司別無選擇，只能接受油價；2026年4至8月亞太航空整體客運量為負數，9月才勉強回到水面之上。

總幹事並未開出具體願望清單，而是敦促各國政府先從比較稅費著手，把本國對航空公司課徵的離境稅、降落費與停機費與鄰國比較，檢視是否合理、是否真正支持航空業。他警告，若燃油價格維持在每桶185美元以上的水準，將難以持續；若油價居高不下，真的可能成為問題，協會最擔心的是雪球效應，即一家航空公司出問題會蔓延到其他業者。大會同時通過4項決議，涵蓋航空永續、旅客權益、客艙安全與航空保安，並重申2030年永續航空燃油使用占比5%的目標，不過永續燃油成本仍為傳統燃油的3至4倍。
